title: When the Horizon Wakes
premise: Edmund Dravenmoor has spent a decade erasing herself from her famous archaeologist father's shadow, working remote river surveys no one wants. When a government team vanishes in the flooded delta, she is the only tracker willing to go after them—dragged into partnership with Casimir Vane, a charming stranger whose commission hides his role as her father's heir-hunter. As the monsoon closes in and the missing team's fate points to an artifact Edmund's father died chasing, she must decide whether to destroy the inheritance that corrupted him or claim it herself. In the end, Edmund sinks the artifact beneath the rising waters, exposes Vane's employers, and chooses anonymity on her own terms—no longer hiding, but free.
about_author: A. M. Iversen is the pen name of a former river-survey cartographer who spent six seasons mapping floodplains across three continents before turning to fiction. Their novels blend field-accurate wilderness survival with slow-burning moral thrillers about what families leave buried.

chapters.title: The River Keeps Its Receipts
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Working a solo survey upriver, Edmund reads water-stained gear abandoned on a sandbar—government issue, no bodies, no tracks. She reports it and is ordered to move on. Emotional beat: unease sharpening into dread as her instinct for reading wilderness says people didn't leave here; they were taken by something that planned.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Levee
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. At the last supply town before the wet season, Casimir Vane finds her: polished boots, wrong questions, a government contract he flashes too readily. He needs a guide into the delta; she needs money for boat repairs. Emotional beat: wary transactional alliance, each sizing the other as either shield or threat.

chapters.title: What the Father Left
chapters.summary: Casimir's POV. Aboard Edmund's leaking boat, Casimir privately reviews his real file: locate Edmund Dravenmoor, sole blood heir of archaeologist Aldous Dravenmoor, dead seven years with his final dig unaccounted for. Emotional beat: Casimir's professional charm cracking against genuine curiosity about the woman who refuses her own name.

chapters.title: Into the Green Throat
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. They push into the flooded forest as the first storm bands arrive. Edmund teaches Casimir survival rules; he proves unexpectedly competent but lies smoothly about small things. They find the survey team's second camp—burned, deliberate. Emotional beat: growing respect braided with sharpening suspicion.

chapters.title: Tracks That End Mid-Stride
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. At the burn site, Edmund reconstructs the night: eight people walked calmly into the water carrying their own packs. No struggle. She finds a carved stone marker matching nothing in any registry—except a sketch in her memory of her father's notebooks. Emotional beat: the past reaching through the mud to touch her.

chapters.title: The Monsoon Closes the Door
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The full monsoon hits; retreat upstream becomes impossible. Holed up in a ruined mission station, Edmund and Casimir trade guarded histories. He offers a half-truth about why he's really here; she gives a half-truth back. Emotional beat: intimacy born of confinement, both lying by omission.

chapters.title: Eight Names, One Survivor
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. In the mission's records Edmund identifies the vanished team's leader—and realizes one name was never on the manifest: a ninth person who joined late. Someone inside the expedition led them out. Emotional beat: betrayal reframing everything; the enemy isn't the wilderness.

chapters.title: The Ninth Man
chapters.summary: Casimir's POV. Casimir admits partial truth: his employers believe Aldous Dravenmoor found the Meridian—a relic his journals call 'a crown for whoever holds it'—and the vanished team was searching when someone went rogue. Casimir confesses he was hired to find Edmund, not the river. Emotional beat: rupture of trust; Edmund walks into the rain alone.

chapters.title: Alone Is a Skill
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Edmund strikes out solo toward her father's last coordinates, which she's carried in her head for years. Flashbacks surface: the estrangement, the letter she never answered, the way power changed Aldous in his final year. Emotional beat: grief and anger braiding into resolve—the dig site is also where her answers live.

chapters.title: What Follows Quietly
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. She realizes she's being followed—not Casimir, but the ninth man, alive and patient. A near-fatal encounter in the flooded ruins ends with her captor wounded and fleeing, dropping a photograph of her father holding the Meridian. Emotional beat: terror transmuting into fury; she stops running.

chapters.title: Reunion at Gunpoint
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Casimir tracks her down, saving her from drowning rather than hunting her—his employers cut him loose when he refused to retrieve Edmund by force. They reconcile without forgiveness: partners of necessity, honest now about the lies. Emotional beat: battered trust rebuilt on truth instead of charm.

chapters.title: The Drowned Dig
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. They reach Aldous's final excavation, half-swallowed by the delta. Inside, evidence shows her father's own crew fractured over the Meridian—one faction wanting it buried, one wanting it sold. Her father sided with burial, too late. Emotional beat: Edmund finally understanding her father not as a legend or a monster, but a man who failed.

chapters.title: Inheritance of Rot
chapters.summary: Casimir's POV. Casimir reads Aldous's journals and sees the pattern: everyone who touches the Meridian begins justifying atrocities within weeks—including, he suspects, the ninth man, once Aldous's most trusted student. Emotional beat: Casimir confronting that his employers don't want to study the relic; they want to wear it.

chapters.title: The Ninth Man's Gospel
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. The ninth man—Marek, Aldous's protégé—captures them at the dig. He doesn't want to sell the Meridian; he believes it chose him, that the vanished team 'went ahead' willingly to prepare its rising. His calm certainty is worse than violence. Emotional beat: horror at how conviction can be indistinguishable from corruption.

chapters.title: The Choice in the Water
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Forced to open the inner vault, Edmund faces the Meridian: beautiful, humming, and already whispering justifications—her grievances, her rightness, her inheritance. She nearly understands Marek. Emotional beat: the theme made flesh; power offering itself as identity.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Edmund shatters the moment by refusing aloud—not destroying it yet, but denying its claim. Marek turns violent; Casimir breaks free; the vault floods as the storm peaks. They escape with the Meridian as the dig collapses behind them. Emotional beat: triumph laced with fear of what she almost became.

chapters.title: Marek's Last Sermon
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Pursued downriver by Marek and the surviving vanished-team members, now his converts, Edmund and Casimir run the flooding rapids in the failing boat. A brutal chase sequence ends with Marek's boat wrecked—but Marek himself unaccounted for. Emotional beat: adrenaline giving way to exhausted clarity about what remains to be done.

chapters.title: What Power Buys
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Waiting out the storm's tail, Edmund interrogates the Meridian's hold on her—she catches herself planning what she could fix, who she could become, with it. Casimir admits his employers will send others. Emotional beat: quiet, terrible honesty; the hardest fight is internal.

chapters.title: The Sinking
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. At the deepest channel of the delta—the place her father marked as 'the grave, if I fail'—Edmund weights the Meridian and sinks it beyond recovery, speaking a eulogy for her father and for the version of herself that wanted it. Emotional beat: catharsis; breaking the inheritance rather than claiming or selling it.

chapters.title: Settlements
chapters.summary: Casimir's POV. Downstream, they intercept his employers' advance team and hand over evidence of Marek's cult and the Meridian's destruction—Casimir burning his bridges deliberately, choosing Edmund's side over his career. Emotional beat: redemption earned through cost, not charm.

chapters.title: Marek, Unfound
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. The epilogue-tension chapter: official searchers find the vanished team's remains and close the case, but Marek's body is never recovered, and one convert is seen alive far north. Edmund chooses not to chase him. Emotional beat: acceptance that some horizons stay dark; vigilance without obsession.

chapters.title: When the Horizon Wakes
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Months later, Edmund takes a new survey contract—not hiding this time, but choosing the work openly, with Casimir as partner. On the river at dawn she watches the horizon lighten and feels no pull toward what sleeps beneath it. Emotional beat: resolution; identity claimed freely, inheritance released, the wilderness forgiven at last.
